newsitem.title: USA: Colgate sees nine pct unit volume growth.
newsitem.headline: Colgate sees nine pct unit volume growth.

text.p: Colgate-Palmolive Co said Thursday it saw worldwide unit volume growth of nine percent in the second quarter of 1997, fueled by strong new product sales and increases in global advertising.

In a press statement announcing second quarter earnings, Chairman and Chief Executive Reuben Mark, said, "Market shares increased in most areas, with new products receiving excellent consumer response. Ongoing cost savings and restructuring drove gross profit margin up 180 basis points, allowing for a worldwide increase in business-building advertising of almost 20 percent, at the same time that earnings grew sharply."

The consumer products giant reported second quarter earnings per share of $0.58, compared with EPS of $0.49 in the second quarter of 1996. Sales increased six percent to $2.3 billion and would have increased nine percent had it not been for the effects of foreign currency translation, the company said.

Colgate said it saw volume growth in every division, with Colgate-Latin America and Hill's Pet Nutrition up 12 percent each, Colgate-Europe up eight percent, Colgate-North America up seven percent and Colgate-Asia/Africa up five percent.
